Build a travel-time graph from road/trail linestrings

Source: R/fn_network.R
build_network.Rd

Build a travel-time graph from road/trail linestrings

Usage

build_network(
  lines,
  road_speed = 30,
  trail_speed = 4,
  snap = 1,
  connect = 50,
  speeds = osm_speeds
)

Arguments

lines

sf LINESTRINGs in a projected CRS (metres), with a class column ("road"/"trail"); osm_access output fits directly.

road_speed, trail_speed

fallback class speeds in km/h (defaults 30, 4) for a highway tag not listed in speeds.

snap

tight grid (metres) that segment endpoints snap to when forming nodes (default 1) - within-class noding, so parallel switchbacks/lanes are not fused.

connect

liberal tolerance (metres, default 50) for bridging a stub end of one class to the nearest node of the other class - i.e. closing trailhead gaps where a trail dead-ends near a road (or a road near a trail) without a shared OSM node. Set 0 to disable. Only degree-1 ends are bridged, so it never fuses same-class features.

speeds

named per-highway speed lookup in km/h (default osm_speeds); each contracted edge is single-highway, so one speed applies. Edge weight is length / speed - change speeds and rebuild (cheap) to re-time without re-pulling or re-contracting.

Value

a list: graph (an undirected igraph with edge weight in hours and class - road/trail/connect, vertex coords x/y) and nodes (data.frame of node name, x, y).
